{"id":"mimid-gn1w","title":"Flake: stock_rust_client's reconnecting-stream wait misses its 15s budget under full-workspace load","design":"Observed 2026-11-25 during a full `cargo test --workspace --all-features`
run. Recorded with the numbers rather than fixed, because the right fix
depends on whether this is only load.

WHAT HAPPENED.

  crates/mimid-agent/tests/stock_rust_client.rs:346
  "a StateChange on the reconnecting stream: Elapsed(())"
  test result: FAILED, finished in 18.97s

The assertion is a tokio::time::timeout(PATIENCE, ...) waiting for an
SseEvent::StateChange on a REOPENED event source, after
`b.post(&chat_b, "one more")`. PATIENCE is 15 seconds
(crates/mimid-agent/tests/common/mod.rs:40).

WHAT I CHECKED, in this order:

  - Re-ran the test alone three times: ok, ok, ok, in 2.58s, 2.80s and
    2.66s. So the whole test takes under three seconds unloaded and the
    one 15-second wait inside it expired under a full-workspace run.
  - Whether my change could have caused it: the work in progress was
    bead mimid-1wgh.129 (a MemberError variant, an AgentError variant,
    Agent::rekey, Store::rekey, a recovery branch in
    vtc_backend::export_media_secret, and documentation). None of it is
    on the event-source, SSE or reconnect path, and none of it runs
    unless a media secret is exported. Not proof, but there is no
    mechanism.
  - Re-ran the full workspace with --no-fail-fast afterwards to confirm
    the suite is otherwise clean.

SO IT IS A TIMING FLAKE UNDER LOAD, roughly a 6x slowdown of one wait on
a machine running many test binaries at once.

WHY NOT JUST RAISE PATIENCE. Because 15 seconds for an event that takes
well under one is already generous, and a budget that fails means
something took 15 seconds, which is worth understanding before it is
hidden. Two things to look at first:

  1. Whether the reopened event source's first StateChange waits on
     something with its own timer (a reconnect backoff, a poll interval)
     that is long relative to PATIENCE. A backoff of a few seconds plus a
     loaded machine would explain a 15-second miss without anything being
     wrong.
  2. Whether this test's fixture is heavy enough to be starved: it runs
     TWO daemons and a server in-process, and the full suite runs many
     such binaries in parallel.

If it turns out to be only contention, the honest fix is a longer
PATIENCE for this one wait with a comment saying why, not a global one.

NOT SEEN BEFORE in this session's several full runs, and not seen again
in the run immediately after, so the rate is low. It will bite CI
eventually.
","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-25T08:52:43.175732111Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-25T08:52:43.175732111Z","labels":["test"]}

{"notes":"2026-11-25: did NOT reproduce in four consecutive full-workspace runs
(cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast), all with
stock_rust_client_chats_through_two_daemons passing. Those runs were on
the same machine on which it failed once at 18.97s against PATIENCE of
15s, and they were not lighter: each was a full rebuild of every test
target after clippy and the rustdoc gate had invalidated the profile.

So the one failure looks load-dependent rather than a defect on the
SSE or reconnect path, and the next person should not go looking for a
bug in that path on the strength of it. What would settle it is a run
under deliberate CPU contention, or the test logging what it was still
waiting for when PATIENCE ran out -- today it says only that it timed
out, which is why one failure told us so little.

Still NOT fixed by raising the timeout. A 15s patience that needs
raising is a thing worth understanding."}

{"notes":"2026-11-25, SECOND OCCURRENCE, and it supports the load hypothesis.

Failed again at crates/mimid-agent/tests/stock_rust_client.rs:346, the
PATIENCE wait, after 35.49s -- against 18.97s the first time and ~2.6s
in isolation. So the overrun grew with the load rather than being a
fixed budget being just missed.

THE LOAD WAS DELIBERATE, if accidentally so: three cargo invocations
were contending for this machine at the time (two full gate runs and a
per-crate check I started on top of them), which is heavier than the
earlier run that failed and much heavier than the four full runs
earlier today that all passed. That is the contention test the previous
note asked for, and the flake reproduced under it.

So: load-dependent, and NOT a defect on the SSE or reconnect path. The
earlier note's advice stands -- do not go looking for a bug there on
the strength of these two failures.

STILL NOT FIXED BY RAISING PATIENCE. What the two failures argue for is
the other half of that note: the test should log what it was still
waiting for when the budget ran out. Both failures say only that it
timed out, which is why two occurrences have narrowed the cause and not
the mechanism."}

{"notes":"2026-11-25: both SSE waits in crates/mimid-agent/tests/stock_rust_client.rs now report what they saw on timeout, so the next occurrence says which bug it is instead of only that it timed out.

The message discriminates the hypotheses: "no frames arrived at all" means the stream never delivered; a list of Unknown(ping) frames means the stream is alive and the change was never sent, which for a stream opened just before the write that causes it is a change published before the subscribe completed -- the EventSource does not replay, so waiting longer cannot help; a StateChange naming other types means the write landed but not for the type under test.

Applied to until_changed as well as the reconnecting-stream wait. They had the same blindness and until_changed is used in several places, so leaving it would mean the next flake there told us as little as this one did.

NOT DONE, and both still open:

* A REPRODUCTION RATE. Pin to one core (taskset -c 0) or run against a parallel build, in a loop, and count failures over 50 runs. Without a rate, "it passed again" proves nothing -- which is the position four passes and two failures leaves us in, and this clean run's pass is worth nothing as evidence either.
* WHETHER THE ASSERTION IS SOUND. The wait requires a StateChange on a stream opened immediately before the write that causes it. JMAP's EventSource has no replay and a client that misses one is expected to notice by state token and re-fetch, so the test may be asserting a guarantee the protocol does not make. If so the fix is in the test -- post after the stream is known live, or assert the resulting state through /get -- and that is Mark's call, because the honest version asserts less than today's does."}
